newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BELGIAN CUP FINAL TACTICAL ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BELGIAN CUP FINAL TACTICAL ANALYSIS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Anderlecht and Ekeren, who meet in the Belgium Cup final at the King Baudouin national stadium on Sunday (1400 GMT):

Playing style: Anderlecht traditionally use a 4-4-2 formation but occasionally shift to 4-3-3. System based on a strong, reliable defence which is now in disarray due to injuries to key players. Several mainstays out and others, including Bosnian libero Suad Katana and Nigerian international Celestine Babayaro doubtful. Anderlecht never adjust tactics to opponents and seldom apply counter-attacking game or off-side trap in league matches.

Strengths: Swedish international Par Zetterberg has played at a consistently high level all season -- described by himself as his best ever -- and boosts quality in midfield. He is also lethal at set-pieces. Wings traditionally well covered by former internationals Danny Boffin and Bruno Versavel. Once ahead, Anderlecht rarely let go of victory.

Weaknesses: Host of injuries and departure of handful of key players, including Belgian internationals Filip De Wilde and Bertrand Crasson, have undermined quality of team, which failed to end in the top two of league for the first time since 1989. Mid-season loss of key striker Gilles De Bilde, banned after punching opponent and moved to PSV Eindhoven, compounded lack of firepower up front. Rejuvenated side always struggles to overcome early deficit.
Motivation: Anderlecht desperately trying to win a prestigious consolation prize to soothe spoiled fans and sponsors who saw their team lift the Belgian title four times in the past seven years.

Playing style: 4-3-3 but system changed "a la carte" to adjust to opponents when team was badly in need of points earlier this season. Sticking to preferred system lately after series of good games, including 4-1 league victory over Anderlecht.

Strengths: Very fast on the break and team has found the right balance after a difficult start to the season due to the fact a high number of newcomers had to be fitted in. Their main asset is Canadian marksman Tomasz Radzinski, scorer of two hat-tricks earlier this month, including one against Anderlecht. Team highly prolific lately, scored 13 goals in three league matches.
Weaknesses: Resistance often crumbles completely if the team faces a two-goal deficit. Can no longer just assume role of underdogs, having beaten Anderlecht 4-1 earlier this month.
Motivation: Always a challenge to beat the likes of Anderlecht. The club claims that winning the Cup is not of vital importance, but first-ever major victory would obviously give financial leeway.
